title: Minkä värisiä: asking about several things
focus: For the colours of several things, use minkä värisiä. Minkä värisiä autot ovat? — Autot ovat punaisia.
targetSkills: Minkä värisiä: asking about several things
prerequisiteSkills: Minkä värinen: asking the colour of one thing

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “What colour are the cars?”
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which. For the colours of several things, use minkä värisiä. Minkä stays unchanged, while värinen becomes värisiä. Minkävärisiä is the corresponding joined spelling. The complete question means “What colour are the cars”.
requiredSkills: Minkä värisiä: asking about several things
exercises.targetSkill: Minkä värisiä: asking about several things

parts.role: question modifier (asks which item or group)
parts.formation: Minkä is the genitive form of mikä and remains unchanged in these descriptive question phrases.

parts.role: colour being asked about
parts.formation: Värinen changes -nen to -siä in plural partitive värisiä.

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Minkä värisiä talot ovat?”: choose “The houses are white.”
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. Describe the ordinary plural group's members with a plural partitive colour adjective: Autot ovat punaisia (“The cars are red”). The taught -nen colour words change -nen to -sia/-siä; other supplied patterns include musta → mustia and vihreä → vihreitä. The complete reply means “The houses are white”.
